chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the menstruating woman make up the Prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'Does she make up the Fast?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'From where does that come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the first one who analogized was Iblis'. I said, 'And the fasting one can submerge in the water?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'. I said, 'So can he wear wet clothes upon his body?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'From where does that come?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From that'. I said, 'Does the fasting one smell the rosemary?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, because it is a pleasure, and it is disliked for him to derive pleasure.'

key_terms.تَقْضِي: She makes up (missed acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a menstruating woman regarding making up prayers and fasting, and what is disliked for a fasting person regarding scents?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the asymmetry in religious obligations, noting that while menstruating women are exempt from prayer, they must make up fasting, a distinction rooted in the concept of 'Qias' (analogical reasoning) attributed to Iblis. It further details specific rulings for the fasting individual, permitting submersion in water but prohibiting deriving pleasure from scents like rosemary, as the essence of fasting is the restraint of sensory enjoyment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The menstruating woman has to make up the (missed) Prayer?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘She has to make up the Fast?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘From where has that come about?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The first one who anlogised was Iblees<sup>la</sup>’. I said, ‘And the Fasting one can stay still in the water?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘So, can he wear wet clothes upon his body?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’. I said, ‘From where has that come about?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From that’. I said, ‘The Fasting one can smell the aromas?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, because he would derive pleasure, and he<sup>asws</sup> disliked it for himself<sup>asws</sup> that he derives pleasure’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Hassan ibn ‘Rashid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if a woman because of Hayd (menses) is required to make Qada’ (compensatory) Salat (prayer). He (the Imam) said, ’No, she is not required.’ I then asked about fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, she must make Qada’ (compensatory fast for) fasting missed during experiencing Hayd (menses).’ I then asked on what basis it is so.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The first one who used analogy was Iblis (Satan).’ I then asked, ‘Can a person fasting stay in water?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so.’ I then asked, ‘Can he wear wet clothes?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’ I then asked, ‘On what basis is this?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is from that (there is no analogizing in religion)’ I asked, ‘Can a fasting person use sweet basil?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, because it is a pleasure which is undesirable to enjoy.’”
